name: Third party safety rating agencies
blurb: Ratings bodies evaluating model safety for underwriting eligibility, on the credit rating pattern.
summary: Ratings bodies evaluating model safety for underwriting eligibility, on the credit rating pattern.

part_3_high_value_red_flags: A professional liability exclusion for rating agency services or credit rating activities that would remove the core exposure from cover.
A definition of professional services that does not include model safety evaluation, red teaming, or algorithmic auditing.
A sublimit for defamation, libel, or slander that is too low to cover a claim from a major AI developer whose model is downgraded.
An exclusion for systemic risk or aggregation of claims arising from the same rating action that would cap coverage for a single flawed methodology.
A prior acts exclusion or retroactive date that cuts off coverage for ratings issued before the current policy period.
A regulatory action exclusion that removes defense costs for investigations by securities or insurance regulators.
A cyber exclusion that would deny coverage if a data breach corrupts the rating model or leaks confidential model information.
manuscript_wording_and_carve_backs: Delete any exclusion for rating agency services and replace it with an affirmative definition of professional services that includes model safety evaluation, algorithmic auditing, and red team reporting.
Add a manuscript endorsement covering regulatory investigations and defense costs for inquiries by insurance or securities regulators, with a sublimit negotiated to at least one million.
Buy back the defamation and trade libel sublimit to match the full professional liability limit, because a low safety rating can destroy an AI developer's market value.
Add a prior acts endorsement with a retroactive date back to the agency's first rating issuance, so that all historical ratings are covered under the new policy.
Include an innocent insured provision so that one employee's fraudulent rating does not void coverage for the agency or other insured persons.
Add a contractual liability extension that covers the agency's assumption of liability in rating service agreements, provided the liability would have attached in tort.
Negotiate a failure to maintain accreditation carve back so that loss of a regulatory license or industry accreditation does not automatically trigger an exclusion.

part_4_program_structure_and_limits.bi_waiting_period: Business interruption waiting period is often twelve to twenty four hours because the agency must issue time sensitive ratings and any outage directly stops revenue.
part_4_program_structure_and_limits.business_interruption: Business interruption coverage should include contingent business interruption for loss of a key data provider or cloud service, with limits tied to the agency's gross revenue over a twelve month indemnity period.
part_4_program_structure_and_limits.property_eb_equipment: Electronic data processing equipment coverage for servers, workstations, and data storage is typically written on a separate schedule with limits based on replacement cost, often one to five million, because the agency's rating platform depends on continuous computing.
part_4_program_structure_and_limits.per_occurrence_primary_excess_layered_pr: Office property coverage is typically layered with a primary limit of five to ten million and excess layers up to the full replacement cost of owned buildings and leasehold improvements, but the rating agency's property values are usually modest compared to its liability exposure.

part_2_paper_type_and_limit_structure.cgl_primary: A modest commercial general liability policy for premises and operations, typically one to two million per occurrence, because the agency's main exposure is professional not bodily injury or property damage.
part_2_paper_type_and_limit_structure.paper_basis: Claims made, because a safety rating agency's errors may not cause insurer losses until years after the rating is issued, and claims made coverage aligns the policy period with when the claim is first made against the agency.
part_2_paper_type_and_limit_structure.excess_umbrella_towers: Follow form excess over the professional liability and general liability policies, with towers often reaching fifty million or more because a single wrong rating could affect multiple insurers and aggregate losses.

part_1_core_third_party_liability_exposu: Professional negligence claims from insurers who relied on an inaccurate safety rating and wrote underpriced or uninsurable AI risks.
Defamation or trade libel claims from AI developers whose models receive a low safety rating that harms their commercial reputation.
Breach of contract claims from AI developers or insurers who allege the rating agency failed to follow its published methodology or deliver the rating on time.
Misrepresentation claims if the rating agency's safety rating is included in offering documents or underwriting submissions and later proves false.
Regulatory enforcement actions if the agency is treated as a credit rating agency and fails to meet registration, disclosure, or conflict of interest rules.
Third party reliance claims from policyholders or investors who claim they relied on the rating to purchase AI insurance or securities.
Intellectual property infringement claims if the rating methodology or reports incorporate proprietary model data without authorization.

underwriter_wants_to_know: The rating agency's methodology for evaluating model safety, including whether it has access to model weights, training data, and red team results.
The independence of the rating agency from AI developers and insurers, including ownership, funding, and any revenue from rated entities.
The contractual limitations of liability in the rating agency's terms of service with insurers and AI developers.
The historical accuracy and dispute record of the agency's ratings, including any past rating changes that led to insurer losses.
The regulatory status of the agency, whether it is registered or overseen like a credit rating agency under securities laws.
The data security and confidentiality controls for the proprietary model information the agency receives during evaluations.
The agency's errors and omissions insurance history, including prior claims and whether any rating has been withdrawn or corrected.
